#  11839 - Case Study Seminar for Management of Modern Value Creation Systems Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **11839 - module is no longer offered from WS 2019/20**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Case Study Seminar for Management of Modern Value Creation Systems**  |  
|  Fallstudienseminar zum Management von modernen Wertschöpfungssystemen   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 3 - Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Energy Systems   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr. rer. soc. oec. Winkler, Herwig 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every summer semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | Through case studies this seminar seeks to engage students with current topics around the management of modern value creation systems. It offers the possibility to generate communicative skills and to acquire managerial expertise while analysing complex problem formulations. Besides the knowledge generated around the technical content, the students will have the opportunity to improve their presentation skills, to become more analytic and to be able to formulate ‘critic-argumentations’ around realistic managerial situations. Therefore, a high degree of autonomy, determination and precision is expected from the students when approaching the seminar’s case studies.  |  
| Contents:  | The Cases presented in the seminar immerse students into realistic situations around the management of modern value creation systems. Cases will be selected to disclose the reality of managerial decision-making – including incomplete information, time constraints, and conflicting goals – giving students the opportunity to learn how to analyse real managerial situations. Additionally, the seminar has been structured to stimulate students' thinking through the encouragement of discussion. As a result, it is expected from the students to come out with innovative solutions to those case studies, which will have to be individually completed under academic specifications. Before the last session, students will have to deliver their work it form of an Essay, which has to enclose each case’s analysis and the closing remarks around the overall topic of the seminar.  |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | 
  * Module _11676 Management of Logistic Systems_
  * Module _11678 Management of Production Systems_

 |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | No successful participation in associated phase-out modules:
  * _11277 Logistikseminar_**AND**
  * _11680 Produktionsseminar_.

 |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Seminar / 2 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 150 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | None  |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 1. Three separate presentations (each max. 15 min) (70%): 
  * Presentation of the analysis regarding the first case study (33%)
  * Presentation of the analysis regarding the first case study (33%)
  * Presentation of the analysis regarding the third case study, Summary and closing remarks around the main theme of the seminar (34%)

2. An essay will have to be delivered at the end of the seminar (max. 10 Pages). The essay should include the analysis carried out for each case of study as well as closure remarks regarding the main theme of the seminar (30%)  |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | 15  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | Follow-up Module to:
  * 11680 Produktionsseminar
  * 11277 Logistikseminar

 |  
| Module Components:  | 
  * Case Study Seminar for management of modern value creation systems (seminar)

 |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Follow-up Module/s:  |  Phase-out module since: 18.06.2019 
  * without Follow-up Module/s
